skill.name: pricing-audit

skill.summary: A structured 30-check audit that turns pricing gaps into a scored, prioritized action plan.

content.value_statement: Pricing reviews often produce opinions without a consistent score or action order. This skill evaluates 30 checks and turns gaps into three prioritized levers and a 90-day remediation plan.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates 30 pricing checks across four defined dimensions.
Scores diagnostic data, reference frames, tier architecture, and operating practice.
Identifies the three highest-priority pricing levers.
Reports pass, partial, fail, or not-applicable status for each check.
limitations: It cannot verify business data that the operator does not provide.
It does not replace customer research, financial analysis, or executive judgment.
It cannot guarantee revenue improvement from any recommended change.
It depends on an accessible pricing page when live page analysis is requested.

use_cases.title: Prepare a pricing review
use_cases.description: Give a pricing leader a consistent baseline before a product, sales, and finance review.

use_cases.title: Prioritize commercial work
use_cases.description: Help a revenue operations team rank pricing gaps by impact, reversibility, and available evidence.

use_cases.title: Challenge a pricing proposal
use_cases.description: Give a founder or product executive a structured way to test tiers, anchors, value metrics, and discount practices.

prompt_templates.title: Run a first audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this B2B pricing program across all 30 checks. Use only the information provided, mark unknowns clearly, and give the overall score.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: starting a structured pricing review.

prompt_templates.title: Review one dimension
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate the diagnostic data dimension using the supplied pricing evidence. List each check as pass, partial, fail, or not applicable, with a short reason.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: investigating data quality before changing prices.

prompt_templates.title: Test tier architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess these pricing tiers against the tier architecture checks. Identify issues with the value metric, decoy, anchor, feature differences, and customer distribution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: reviewing a proposed packaging and pricing page.

prompt_templates.title: Build the 90-day plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the completed audit to select the three strongest pricing levers. Sequence the work over 90 days and define an owner, action, timeline, and success metric for each.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: converting audit results into an operating plan.

output_examples.input: A B2B company has recent willingness-to-pay research, unclear tier outcomes, and no documented discount approvals.
output_examples.output: Overall score: 64/100. Top levers: define tier outcomes, document discount thresholds, and connect renewal increases to a standard cadence.

output_examples.input: A pricing page shows four tiers, mixed per-seat and usage metrics, and no visible prices below the enterprise level.
output_examples.output: Tier architecture: fail. The review flags inconsistent value measurement, excessive tier count, and missing price transparency as the first remediation priorities.

output_examples.input: A team provides a full audit with failed checks and asks what to do first.
output_examples.output: 90-day order: validate willingness to pay, simplify the tier structure, then test outcome-focused copy. Each lever includes an owner and measurable success criterion.

best_practices: Provide current pricing data, customer segments, and test results before requesting a score.
Separate confirmed evidence from assumptions and mark unknown checks as not applicable only with a reason.
Sequence recommendations so foundational research precedes tier or copy changes.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the score as a forecast of revenue or margin.
Do not change tiers before checking the underlying value metric and customer evidence.
Do not present unsupported assumptions as completed pricing research.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits 30 checks across diagnostic data, reference frames and copy, tier architecture, and operating practice.

faq.question: What does the score mean?
faq.answer: The score summarizes the supplied evidence against the framework. It is a diagnostic signal, not a revenue forecast.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide pricing data, customer segment details, tier information, discount practices, research results, and relevant page content.

faq.question: Can it review a live pricing page?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a pricing page URL when live page analysis is available, and the skill can assess tiers, copy, and value metrics.

faq.question: Does it recommend new prices?
faq.answer: It prioritizes pricing improvements and tests. It does not invent price points without supporting customer and business evidence.

faq.question: Who should use the results?
faq.answer: Pricing, revenue operations, product, sales, finance, and executive teams can use the results to coordinate a pricing improvement plan.
